title: Converge routing state and metrics adapters to eliminate lock storms
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Under sustained high QPS (>30k req/s) we observe p99 request latency spikes originating in the smart routing hotpath. Root cause analysis points to global routing-state locks and duplicated region-affinity caches plus blocking metric adapter calls that amplify contention. Secondary issues: an older Redis client (v6.x) and an older Go runtime (1.20) are preventing use of newer non-blocking primitives and connection pooling improvements.

Goal: Reduce routing hotpath contention and p99 latency by refactoring the routing state machine and metric adapters so reads are lock-free and writes are sharded; remove duplicated region-affinity caches; upgrade Redis client and Go where required. Success criteria: p99 tail latency improvement of >= 30% on our synthetic high-QPS benchmark, 10% reduction in lock contention traces, no customer-facing errors during canary.

Proposed approach: 1) Introduce a sharded routing-state store keyed by region-shard (configurable shard count) and implement an RCU-style read path so the common-case read path avoids mutex acquisition. 2) Replace blocking metric adapter calls in the hotpath with a non-blocking, batched telemetry writer with backpressure-aware sampling. 3) Remove duplicate region-affinity caches by collapsing to a single canonical cache in routing-core and exposing a minimal read-only view to other subsystems. 4) Upgrade Redis client from redis/v6 to redis/v8 and bump Go from 1.20 -> 1.22 to avail of runtime contention and network improvements. 5) Add detailed tracing and new metrics (lock_acquire_ns, shard_miss_count, telemetry_queue_lat_ns) to verify behavior.

Trade-offs and risks: - Increasing shard count improves write throughput but increases memory and complexity. - RCU-style approach complicates write paths and GC semantics (we must be explicit about object lifetimes). - Redis client upgrade requires validation of connection pool behaviour in dedicated vs. hosted environments. - There is a small risk of metric loss during the transition to batched telemetry writer; mitigated by durability to disk in the writer for short windows and fallbacks.

Rollout plan: implement behind a config-driven feature flag. Canary in a single low-traffic region for 24h with synthetic load tests. If success, expand to high-traffic region for 48h. Maintain automatic rollback if error-rate or latency exceeds thresholds in the SLO runbook.

Telemetry & verification: baseline and post-change A/B benchmarks (links below). New dashboards for lock_acquire_ns per shard, telemetry_outstanding_items, region_affinity_consistency_check.

Docs & follow-ups: internal design doc and migration checklist linked below. Post-mortem/lessons after full rollout.
comments: 2026-02-17 - Asha: Initial RFC posted. Called out three alternatives for the read-path: global mutex + caching, optimistic CAS updates, and RCU-sharded store. We landed on RCU-sharded store after perf modeling. Link to RFC in links.

2026-02-22 - Marco: Started PoC for a 16-shard state store. Microbenchmarks show mutex hold time reduced by ~4.2x on synthetic workload with 80% reads. POC branch: github.com/redwood-inference/routing/poc/sharded-state.

2026-02-28 - Eng review: Bethany (ID) reviewed PoC and requested clearer invariants around object lifetime and GC behavior; created follow-up ENG-18801 for GC testing matrix. Also asked for Canary rollback criteria to be explicit in the ticket.
2026-03-03 - Marco: Implemented non-blocking telemetry writer; added disk-backed spool as short-term durability. Benchmarks show telemetry writer removes ~12% of observed blocking calls in hotpath.
2026-03-06 - QA: Integration smoke tests in staging passed. Noted increase in memory transient on writes; tuning shard count reduced max RSS within acceptable bounds. See staging dashboard link.

2026-03-09 - Security: Quick dependency scan flagged redis/v8 minor CVE-free advisory; security confirmed acceptable but requested upgrade plan for dedicated/private customers — added note to runbook.
2026-03-10 - Marco: Opened PR #5423 for core refactor and PR #5424 for telemetry writer. Both are in review; performance tests attached. Planning canary next week behind feature flag.
